cues: Mrs. Baroda is a little provoked: her husband Gaston has invited an old college friend, Gouvernail, a journalist, to stay on their sugar plantation.
She wanted rest, and her husband to herself.
She has never met the man, but she imagines him, tall, cynical, in eyeglasses, and on that evidence, which is no evidence at all, she dislikes him.
